newsitem.title: USA: Aetna sees HMO pricing up 3-5 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Aetna sees HMO pricing up 3-5 pct in 1997.

text.p: Aetna Inc said it expects 1997 pricing increases of three to five percent for HMO products and four to six percent in point of service.
Pricing for preferred provider organizations is expected to increase five to seven percent and indemnity pricing is expected to increase seven to 12 percent, Aetna said.
An Aetna spokeswoman said about 50 percent of its business renews in January and with about 75 to 80 percent of the data counted, "the prices appear to be sticking."
Overall enrollment growth declined slightly in 1996 because of a large contract that did not renew. But excluding that contract, enrollment rose about four percent, Aetna said.
Commercial HMO enrollment rose about 18 percent and point of service enrollment rose about 25 percent, she said.
For 1997, Aetna said it was targeting commercial and Medicare HMO risk membership growth in the mid-teens.
